solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Morally corrupt equivalent of ten depressions?

parts.note: deca- is the Greek prefix meaning ten, as in decade or decathlon
a dent is a small hollow pressed into a surface; the clue counts ten of them, as in mono-dent, duo-dent and so on

explanation.surface: A question about what ten depressions add up to, set beside a moral judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' flags a playful word-building: the answer read as deca-dent is a made-up name for ten dents.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone in moral decline, self-indulgent and debauched, is described this way.

clue.text: Daughters without refinement are attractive?

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees and records
raw means crude, unprocessed, lacking polish

explanation.surface: A rather catty remark that unpolished daughters still win admirers.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull people in, as a show pulls a crowd, is the verb sense here; the plural matches 'are'.

clue.text: Nurse Carol naturally enters senior partner's practice?

parts.note: to cradle is to nurse, holding a baby in the arms

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, as a person enters a room

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully
natch is slang short for naturally, meaning of course

explanation.surface: A nurse called Carol joins the practice of a senior partner in a medical firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurse Carol' reads as a person's name and job, but 'Carol' is the verb sing. 'Senior partner' is not a firm's boss but an older person in a relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: taking a much younger lover is the habit of an older partner, hence the cryptic hint in the question mark.

clue.text: Tidy black-clad punk getting around to canine

parts.note: to do one's hair or a room is to tidy it up

indicators.note: the goth wraps round the little word, as a person gets round an obstacle

parts.note: a goth is a member of the post-punk subculture known for black clothing

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up a punk in black who gets round to a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a canine is the pointed eye tooth, also called by this name.

clue.text: Twangy part for musician, as always

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is used, the letters running across musician, as and always

explanation.surface: A musician who always takes the twangy part.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a twangy voice resonates through the nose, the sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Result of laying hold firmly

definitions.meaning: a set of eggs laid by a hen at one time

explanation.surface: What comes of laying hold of something firmly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs 'laying hold' together as one phrase; split it after 'laying', which here means producing eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a brood of eggs laid together, and the verb meaning to grasp tightly.

clue.text: See that vessel where hippies got it on

parts.note: lo is an archaic exclamation meaning look or see
a vein is a blood vessel

explanation.surface: Look at the boat where hippies made love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a boat, but it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a 1960s gathering of hippies celebrating peace and free affection was exactly such a place.

clue.text: Month Robert worked round old queen like a natural

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the queen's name
the letters are worked into a new shape, like clay

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
Anne was Queen of Great Britain from 1702 to 1714

explanation.surface: Robert spends a month working on an old queen's portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' is the anagram signal and 'round' the container signal; Queen Anne, who died in 1714, is the usual old queen in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone who acts as if born to a role behaves with natural ease, like a natural.

clue.text: List containing lines informed gang member

indicators.note: the leaning word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a ship that lists or heels leans to one side
L is an abbreviation for line, doubled for lines
to sing is slang for informing to the police

explanation.surface: A list of names, with an informer's lines, that names a gang member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' looks like a register; it is the nautical verb for leaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a member of the notorious motorcycle club is a classic gang member.

clue.text: Answer Scottish island charge after mounting, baseless fear

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing upwards means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides
a rap is a criminal charge, as in beat the rap

explanation.surface: A charge for climbing on a Scottish island causes groundless worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns A + IONA + RAP upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an irrational suspicion of persecution is a fear without basis.

clue.text: Drunk again, ale's numbing pain

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drinking ale again to dull the ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' rearranges AGAIN ALES.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical term: it means loss of sensitivity to hurt, so the deadening of suffering.

clue.text: Key discussion curtailed after six

indicators.note: the shortened word comes after the numeral

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: a tail is cut off, so the last letter of the word for discussion goes

parts.note: talk is discussion

explanation.surface: An important talk cut short after six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' cuts the K from TALK.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something key is essential or crucial.

clue.text: Seconds from parching, planters use borehole as well

indicators.note: the second letter is taken from each of the four following words

explanation.surface: Planters in a parched land also turn to a borehole for water.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: it means in addition, too, besides.

clue.text: Field expertise reduced amount of green growth

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow

indicators.note: the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: finesse is refined skill

explanation.surface: Expert care of a field yields a quantity of greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' trims the last E from FINESSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the state of having many leaves, so a measure of foliage.

clue.text: Bust in Paris, our rising British author

parts.note: the bust is the chest

indicators.note: in a down clue, the French word reads upwards

parts.note: notre is French for our

explanation.surface: A sculpted bust of a British writer goes up in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' suggests sculpture but means the torso. 'rising' turns NOTRE into ERTON.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: G. K. Chesterton was an English writer, creator of Father Brown.

clue.text: Pause to rest, stopping the man endlessly busy working

indicators.note: the word for rest plugs a gap in the other pieces, like a stopper

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: at it means busy, hard at work
on means working, as a machine is on
to sit is to rest

explanation.surface: Taking a pause to rest stops a man from being endlessly busy at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' is the phrase AT IT, which 'endlessly' trims; 'stopping' means the rest word plugs the gap, so it sits inside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a brief delay before acting or speaking is a pause.

clue.text: Cut yarn number in loom

indicators.note: the word for yarn is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: thread is spun yarn
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A weaver cuts yarn for a number of threads in a loom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loom' looks like the weaving frame but is the verb. 'Cut' drops the D of THREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: danger that looms is impending, menacing like a gathering storm.

clue.text: Something to drive about India without success

indicators.note: the vehicle goes about the letter

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Driving around India and failing to get anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something done in vain is done to no avail.

clue.text: Unemployment I should lower, ending four points up

parts.note: I'd is short for I should or I would

indicators.note: the last four letters, which are all compass points, are turned upwards in this down clue

parts.note: to lessen is to lower or reduce

explanation.surface: Someone vows to bring down joblessness, with four points up at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending four points up' turns only SSEN of LESSEN into NESS: S, S, E, N are all compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: having no work, being out of a job, is a state of inactivity.

clue.text: Chews over new leaves — hot stuff?

indicators.note: the letter departs from the word
the word is turned over, read back to front

parts.note: gnaws means chews

explanation.surface: An animal chews over fresh leaves that taste spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns GNAWS into SWANG; 'leaves' drops its N. 'leaves' looks like foliage but is the verb of going.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: stolen goods are hot, so a thief's loot is hot stuff.

clue.text: Money to protect king and knight in great urban moves?

indicators.note: the money surrounds the king, guarding it

parts.note: bread is slang for money
K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: the knight sits inside the word for great

parts.note: ace is slang for excellent
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A chess-like scene: money guards king and knight in great moves.
explanation.walkthrough: King, knight and moves conjure chess, but the moves are dance moves.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the acrobatic street dance born in New York's hip-hop scene consists of city moves.

clue.text: Shade from screen infused with exotic oil

indicators.note: the checking word takes the rearranged letters into it

parts.note: to vet is to screen or check

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shade made from a screen soaked in exotic oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen' suggests a display, but it is the verb to check; 'exotic' scrambles the oil, and 'infused with' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a purple-blue colour is one shade among many.

clue.text: Originally eaten in Mexico, not a thing with mostly cold filling?

definitions.text: Originally eaten in Mexico, not a thing with mostly cold filling?

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter of eaten
the shortened word fills the Spanish word for nothing

parts.note: nada is Spanish for nothing, as spoken in Mexico

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, dropping its last letter

parts.note: chill means cold

explanation.surface: A Mexican dish that was first eaten there, filled with a little chilli.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the cold word and 'filling' puts it inside the Spanish for nothing; the whole clue also describes the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue paints a Mexican tortilla dish, rolled round a filling with chilli sauce.

clue.text: Famous dancer doesn't have heart or foot moving

indicators.note: the middle letter and the last letter of the dancer's name go; in a down clue, the foot is the bottom letter

parts.note: Fred Astaire was a famous Hollywood dancer

explanation.surface: A famous dancer, without heart or foot, can't really dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of ASTAIRE is its middle A; its foot is the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone up and about, in motion, is moving.

clue.text: Told office to exclude British — for their neighbours' funding?

indicators.note: told means said aloud, so the letters are what is heard

parts.note: an office is a bureau; excluding B for British leaves a sound like you-roe

explanation.surface: An office is told to leave out Britain from European funding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to exclude' drops B from BUREAU; 'Told' gives what is heard: UREAU, which sounds like the answer. Seen from Britain, the neighbours are the Continental Europeans.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency of most EU states is the money of Britain's Continental neighbours.

clue.text: Unimpressive million in advance, once

parts.note: ere is an archaic word for before

explanation.surface: A million paid in advance once looked unimpressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something trifling, nothing more than it seems, is unimpressive.

clue.text: Literarily, it's going to weave

definitions.meaning: a literary contraction of it will, with an apostrophe at the front
a fabric with diagonal ribs, made by a particular weave

explanation.surface: A literary declaration that weaving is about to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the poetic contraction of 'it will', and a ribbed cloth weave.

clue.text: Piece of meat where rest can be had in dish before main course

indicators.note: the bed goes inside the dish

parts.note: an entree, in British use, is a dish served before the main course
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A cut of meat served where diners rest before the main course.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a boned steak cut from between the ribs is one such cut of beef.

clue.text: Deny women's being released from old prison

indicators.note: the letter is let out of the prison's name

parts.note: Newgate was a notorious London prison, closed in 1902
W is an abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Authorities deny that women are being freed from the old jail.
explanation.walkthrough: NEWGATE was a notorious prison in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to nullify or contradict a claim is to deny it.

clue.text: Being There, for which acting needs time given over to Sellers' lead

indicators.note: the time letter has to be handed over, replaced by another

parts.note: pretence is acting or pretending

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A trivia question on the film Being There, which needed time devoted to Peter Sellers' starring role.
explanation.walkthrough: Being There is a 1979 film starring Peter Sellers; here the title is simply the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the state of being somewhere, attending in person.
